senses.definition: One who, or a device that, mixes or merges things together.

quotes.text: I had seen so many people all my life—I was an average mixer, but more than average in a tendency to identify myself, my ideas, my destiny with those of all classes that I came in contact with.
quotes.reference: 1936 February, F. Scott Fitzgerald, “The Crack-Up”, in Esquire, retrieved 30 Nov 2020:

quotes.text: Bad mixer as he was, he preferred to be "out of it" in a crowd than out of it altogether.
quotes.reference: 1950, Mervyn Peake, Gormenghast, London: Eyre & Spottiswoode, →OCLC:

senses.definition: A machine outfitted with (typically blunt) blades with which it mixes or beats ingredients in a bowl below.
A nonalcoholic drink (such as lemonade, Coca-Cola or fruit juice) that is added to spirits to make cocktails.
examples: Do we have any mixers? I don't want to drink this vodka neat.

senses.definition: (US) A dance or other social event meant to foster new acquaintances, as at the beginning of a school year.

quotes.text: To encourage those IRL meetings, Thursday hosts events in London and New York, the two cities where it is up and running; the mixer at Hair of the Dog was its eighth in this city and drew a crowd of about 450.
quotes.reference: 2022 January 27, Becky Hughes, “The Hot New Thing in Dating? Actually Going on Dates.”, in The New York Times, →ISSN:

senses.definition: Any of various social dances involving frequent changes of partners.
A device for combining hot and cold water before it emerges from a single spout or shower head.
(electronics) A nonlinear electrical circuit that creates new frequencies from two signals applied to it.
A chiropractor who uses other treatments in addition to spinal adjustment.
